 The Washington Wizards will start Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Alex Sarr, and Deandre Ayton against Hawks on Friday. 
 Anthony Davis is out with an ankle injury, so instead of starting Bilal Coulibaly who started in Dybantsa’s absence, the Wizards have elected to start Ayton at center. This is part of the reason they brought him in last summer, so if he’s available in a redraft league, he could be worth a stream. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis (ankle) is questionable to play against the Hawks on Friday. 
 Davis tweaked his ankle in the first quarter against Atlanta on Wednesday, but he was able to play through it and ended up having a strong night. If he isn’t able to suit up in Friday’s rematch, Deandre Ayton would likely slide into the starting unit. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis took advantage of the Hawks’ size with 26 points (12-of-19 FGs, 2-of-2 FTs), 10 rebounds, three assists and three blocks in a loss. 
 He did tweak his ankle in the first quarter which will be something to monitor if it flares up but it didn’t impact him much in this game. He took advantage of his size over the Hawk’s smaller big men and had a good game. The next game the Wizards play is against the Hawks in Atlanta, so if he’s healthy, it’s possible that he has a similar performance against them on Friday. 
 Alex Sarr 
 WAS 
 Center 
 #20 
 Alex Sarr (knee) is questionable for Wednesday’s game against the Hawks. 
 Sarr did not play in Monday’s win over the Magic, with Deandre Ayton moving into the starting lineup and playing 24 minutes. He should take on a similar workload if Sarr remains out on Wednesday. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis had 27 points (12-of-17 FGs, 2-of-2 FTS), nine rebounds, one assist, three steals and one three-pointer in the Wizards’ 103-94 victory over the Magic on Monday. 
 Davis has now scored at least 25 points and at least nine rebounds in three of his last four games. The 33-year-old center had played in 71 games in the previous three seasons entering this year, but his production has been solid. While Davis’ injury history casts doubt over his durability going forward, he’s been a big part of the Wizards going 4-3 in the early part of the season.

 With Alex Sarr (ankle) sidelined, Ayton will get the starting nod at center. Ayton hasn’t been productive as a reserve this season, though this starting opportunity should allow him to have a solid outing.

 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis had himself a night with 25 points (8-of-18 FGs, 9-of-10 FTs), 13 rebounds, one assist, one steal and a block in Friday’s win over the Hornets. 
 Anthony Davis has imposed his will on the Hornets centers in this game, and they couldn’t do much to stop him. The defense on the big men was good, and he got to the line frequently. It was another great performance from AD and his value should be stable barring injury. The Wizards are winning and he’s a big reason for that. If you’re worried about the injuries, it might be worth exploring the market, but it’s also likely everyone else is just as scared about him. 
 Anthony Davis 
 WAS 
 Forward-Center 
 #23 
 Anthony Davis tallied 18 points (8-of-18 FGs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Wednesday’s loss to the Cavaliers. 
 After shooting 50 percent from the field and scoring 29 points in Monday’s loss to the Hornets, Davis cooled off a bit on Wednesday. Of course, it was a challenging matchup, as the Cavaliers could send either Evan Mobley or Jarrett Allen at Davis for most of the night. AD finished with a complete stat line, but it was surprising that he didn’t attempt a single free throw in 34 minutes of play.

 RJ Barrett supplied 27 points (9-of-21 FGs, 9-of-11 FTs), seven rebounds and five assists over 37 minutes to propel the Raptors to a 121-107 win over the Bucks on Friday.
 Barrett was tasked with shouldering more of the scoring workload in this one with Kawhi Leonard (knee), Scottie Barnes (groin) and Immanuel Quickly (hamstring) out due to injuries. The 26-year-old hoisted a team-leading 21 shot attempts and got to the free-throw line regularly against a struggling Milwaukee squad. He’ll continue to be relevant for fantasy managers as Toronto’s primary offensive catalyst until the rest of their starting lineup gets healthy.
 -  George Bissell

 Jaden McDaniels tallied 23 points (8-of-19 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), six rebounds, five assists, one steal, two blocks and two three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Expected by many to provide added value as a scorer in the aftermath of Anthony Edwards’ knee surgery, things have not worked out that way for McDaniels. He’s scored at least 20 points in two of the Timberwolves’ last six games, hitting 23 in both instances. Against the Pelicans, McDaniels supplemented the scoring output with a complete stat line, which was good news for fantasy managers. He’ll look to post back-to-back games with at least 20 points for the first time this season when the Timberwolves host the Jazz on Sunday.

 Jamal Shead contributed 10 points (4-of-10 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), three rebounds, 16 assists and two steals over 34 minutes in a win over the Bucks on Friday.
 It’s one of the more unusual double-doubles that fantasy managers are going to see all year. Shead dished out a whopping 16 helpers as Toronto pulled away late with an impressive second-half effort against a subpar Milwaukee squad that has just one win through nine games. The 24-year-old was inserted into Toronto’s starting lineup with both Immanuel Quickley (hamstring) and Scottie Barnes (groin) on the shelf with injuries. He’s a bit of a one-category specialist, but he’s a worthwhile streamer in deeper fantasy leagues when he gets the opportunity to start.
 -  George Bissell

 LaMelo Ball recorded 22 points (7-of-15 FGs, 5-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, eight assists and three three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pelicans.
 After his poor showing in an October 28 loss to the Warriors, Ball has scored at least 20 points in three straight games and four of his last five. Coming off a game in which he committed seven turnovers, the Timberwolves point guard did a better job of valuing the basketball on Friday. Ball committed three turnovers on Friday and shot a respectable field-goal percentage. With Anthony Edwards (knee) out, Minnesota has less margin for error, especially in the turnover category. The Timberwolves end their week with a game against the Jazz on Sunday.
 -  Raphielle Johnson

 Alijah Martin went off for 27 points (9-of-11 FGs, 3-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, two steals and one block over 31 minutes in a win over the Bucks on Friday.
 Martin delivered a sublime performance off Toronto’s bench, knocking down six of seven from three-point range, while only missing two of his 11 attempts from the floor. Sometimes, it’s just your night. The 24-year-old former second-round pick didn’t reach double digits in points or minutes through Toronto’s first eight games of the year. He can be safely ignored in all fantasy leagues, but this was the type of performance that figures to lead to increased opportunities moving forward.
 -  George Bissell

 Ayo Dosunmu accounted for 26 points (8-of-14 FGs, 6-of-6 FTs), two rebounds, four assists, one block and four three-pointers in Friday’s win over the Pelicans.
 Dosunmu has scored 21 points or more in three of his six starts since the Timberwolves lost Anthony Edwards (knee), and he’s had at least 15 in all six. Friday’s performance was excellent, as the Timberwolves guard shot the ball efficiently. Over 50 percent from the field, Dosunmu shot 4-of-6 from beyond the arc. He’s currently exceeding his preseason ADP (114) by a significant margin, and at this rate, Dosunmu is on track to be one of the steals of fantasy basketball this season.
 -  Raphielle Johnson
